domains.Networking Concepts: The OSI Model: Not Just Theory

items.q: You are troubleshooting a network issue where a workstation cannot reach the internet. You can successfully ping the default gateway (192.168.1.1) but cannot ping 8.8.8.8. Which OSI layer is most likely where the issue resides?
items.exp: Because you can reach the local gateway, Layer 1 and 2 are functioning. The failure to route traffic beyond the local subnet to an external IP indicates a Layer 3 (Network) routing issue at the gateway/firewall.

items.q: Which of the following IPv4 addresses is a valid loopback address used for local testing?
items.exp: 127.0.0.1 is the standard IPv4 loopback address. 169.254.x.x is APIPA, and 10.x.x.x/192.168.x.x are private IP ranges.

items.q: A network administrator needs to assign an IPv6 address to a router interface that will only be routable within the local site, not across the internet. Which IPv6 prefix should be used?
items.exp: FD00::/8 (Unique Local Address) is the IPv6 equivalent of a private IPv4 address. FE80::/10 is link-local (only on the local segment). 2000::/3 is global unicast, and FF00::/8 is multicast.

items.q: Which routing protocol uses the Shortest Path First (Dijkstra) algorithm and groups routers into areas to limit routing update traffic?
items.exp: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state routing protocol that uses Dijkstra's algorithm and hierarchical areas (like Area 0) to scale efficiently.

items.q: At which layer of the OSI model does a standard, unmanaged network switch operate?
items.exp: A standard switch operates at Layer 2 (Data Link) and forwards frames based on MAC addresses.

items.q: A technician is mapping out the ports required for secure remote administration and file transfer. Which ports should be allowed through the firewall for SSH and SFTP?
items.exp: Both SSH (Secure Shell) and SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) operate over TCP Port 22.

items.q: Which Wi-Fi standard introduced MU-MIMO (Multi-User Multiple Input Multiple Output) and operates exclusively in the 5 GHz band?
items.exp: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates only in the 5 GHz band and introduced downlink MU-MIMO.

items.q: A network engineer wants to logically separate the Accounting department's traffic from the HR department's traffic on the same physical switch. What technology should they implement?
items.exp: Virtual LANs (VLANs) segment a physical switch into multiple logical networks at Layer 2, isolating broadcast domains.

items.q: When configuring a trunk link between two Cisco switches to carry multiple VLANs, which protocol is typically used to tag the frames?
items.exp: IEEE 802.1Q is the industry-standard networking protocol used to tag frames with their VLAN ID over trunk links.

items.q: A company is opening a new branch office and needs a cost-effective way to connect the branch network to the headquarters securely over the public internet. Which implementation is BEST?
items.exp: A Site-to-Site VPN creates a secure, encrypted tunnel over the internet between two routers/firewalls, connecting the entire branch network to HQ cost-effectively.

items.q: To combine the bandwidth of three 1 Gbps switch ports into a single 3 Gbps logical link, which protocol should the network engineer use?
items.exp: LACP (802.3ad) allows multiple physical links to be bundled together to form a single logical link for increased bandwidth and redundancy.

items.q: A technician is terminating a Cat6 cable and needs to ensure it follows the TIA/EIA-568B standard. Which wire color should be placed in pin 1?
items.exp: In the T568B standard, Pin 1 is White/Orange. In T568A, Pin 1 is White/Green.

items.q: A network administrator wants to monitor the bandwidth utilization and interface errors on a core router from a central dashboard. Which protocol is designed for this?
items.exp: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to collect metrics (like bandwidth and CPU usage) and configure network devices centrally.

items.q: Which type of documentation provides a visual representation of how devices are physically connected, including port numbers and cable types?
items.exp: A physical network diagram shows the actual hardware, cabling, and physical layout of the network. A logical diagram shows IP addresses, subnets, and routing.

items.q: The network team is planning to update the firmware on the core distribution switches. To minimize disruption, they plan to do this at 2:00 AM on a Sunday. What process are they following?
items.exp: Change management is the formal process of planning, reviewing, testing, and scheduling changes (like firmware updates during a maintenance window) to minimize risk.

items.q: Which metric describes the average amount of time a network device operates before it experiences a hardware failure?
items.exp: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) measures reliability—the average time a device runs before breaking down.

items.q: A network engineer wants to prevent unauthorized switches from being connected to the corporate network and causing a spanning tree loop. Which feature should be enabled on the access ports?
items.exp: BPDU Guard disables a port if it receives a Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) from an unauthorized switch, protecting the Spanning Tree topology.

items.q: An organization wants to authenticate users connecting to the wireless network using their Active Directory credentials rather than a shared password. Which protocol should the WPA2-Enterprise network use to communicate with the authentication server?
items.exp: RADIUS is the standard protocol used by wireless access points to forward authentication requests to a central server (like NPS or ISE) in a WPA2/3-Enterprise setup.

items.q: Which network security tool is placed inline on the network and actively drops packets that match the signature of a known SQL injection attack?
items.exp: An Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) is inline and actively blocks threats. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) only monitors and alerts.

items.q: To prevent rogue DHCP servers from handing out incorrect IP addresses and gateways to clients, which switch feature must be implemented?
items.exp: DHCP Snooping categorizes switch ports as trusted or untrusted. It drops DHCP Offer messages originating from untrusted ports (where end users sit).

items.q: A firewall has three allow rules (TCP 80, TCP 443 and TCP 5432) and no rule that blocks anything, yet inbound traffic on every other port is still dropped. What principle is this?
items.exp: Implicit Deny is a firewall rule (usually invisible at the bottom of the ACL) that blocks all traffic that wasn't explicitly allowed by higher rules.

items.q: A user's workstation has the IP address 169.254.12.45. They cannot reach the internet or local servers, but the link light on their NIC is solid green. What is the MOST likely cause?
opts: The DHCP server is unreachable or out of addresses
The default gateway is configured incorrectly
items.exp: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) address. The OS assigns this to itself when it asks for an IP via DHCP and receives no response. Since the link light is on, the physical connection (cable) is fine.

items.q: An engineer replaces a failed 10G SFP+ module with a new one. The link comes up, but the interface shows a massive number of CRC errors and dropped frames. The cable is a 200-meter multimode fiber run. What is the MOST likely issue?
items.exp: CRC errors and dropped frames on a fiber link, assuming the link is actually up, usually point to dirty fiber ends, a bad bend radius, or attenuation causing signal degradation. Reversed Tx/Rx would result in the link not coming up at all.

items.q: Users report they can reach websites by typing IP addresses (e.g., 8.8.8.8) into their browser, but not by typing domain names (e.g., google.com). Which protocol is failing?
items.exp: DNS (Domain Name System) resolves human-readable domain names to IP addresses. If IP addresses work but domains don't, DNS is the point of failure.

items.q: A network technician suspects that a router is dropping packets due to congestion. Which command-line tool will trace the path the packets take and report latency/loss at each hop?
items.exp: tracert (Windows) or traceroute (Linux/Cisco) shows the route packets take to a destination, displaying latency and timeouts for every router (hop) along the way.

items.q: Two newly configured switches are connected via a trunk link. Switch A has native VLAN 1, and Switch B has native VLAN 99. What issue will occur?
items.exp: A native VLAN mismatch occurs when the two ends of a trunk link are configured with different native VLANs. This causes untagged frames to leak into the wrong VLAN, breaking connectivity and generating CDP/LLDP error logs.

items.q: Which wireless standard operates simultaneously on the 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz bands to drastically increase throughput and reduce latency?
items.exp: Wi-Fi 6E extends the 802.11ax standard to include the 6 GHz frequency band, offering wider channels and less interference.

items.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for logical addressing and routing?
items.exp: Layer 3 (Network) uses logical addresses (like IP addresses) to route packets between different networks.

items.q: If an administrator is troubleshooting a problem where two switches are creating an endless broadcast storm, which OSI layer is primarily involved?
items.exp: Layer 2 (Data Link) handles MAC addresses and switching. Broadcast storms and switching loops (mitigated by Spanning Tree Protocol) occur here.

items.q: At which layer of the OSI model does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) operate to ensure reliable data delivery?
items.exp: Layer 4 (Transport) is responsible for end-to-end communication, utilizing protocols like TCP for reliable delivery and UDP for fast, connectionless delivery.

items.q: Which protocol prevents switching loops in a Layer 2 network?
items.exp: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) blocks redundant links to prevent broadcast storms and loops.

items.q: Which routing protocol is an exterior gateway protocol used to route traffic across the internet?
items.exp: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is the protocol that makes the internet work by routing between different autonomous systems.

items.q: What is the purpose of an ARP request?
opts: Resolve a domain name to an IP
Resolve an IP address to a MAC address
Assign an IP address to a client
items.exp: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) broadcasts an IP to find the associated physical MAC address on a local network.

items.q: Which SNMP component stores information about the managed device?
items.exp: The Management Information Base (MIB) is the database on the agent that stores metrics and configuration data.

items.q: What is the term for a snapshot of network performance under normal working conditions?
items.exp: A baseline is established during normal operation so you have a reference point to detect anomalies later.

items.q: Which protocol is used to send log messages to a centralized server?
items.exp: Syslog (port 514) sends event messages to a centralized logging server.

items.q: Which switch feature ensures that only a specific MAC address can communicate on a port?
items.exp: Port security restricts input to an interface by limiting the MAC addresses of the stations allowed to access the port.

items.q: Which IPsec protocol provides data confidentiality (encryption)?
items.exp: Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) encrypts the payload for confidentiality, whereas Authentication Header (AH) only provides integrity.

items.q: What port is typically used for a secure HTTPS web interface?
items.exp: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 for encrypted web traffic.

items.q: Which command shows the MAC address of the local machine on Windows?
items.exp: ipconfig /all displays full TCP/IP configuration for all adapters, including the physical (MAC) address.

items.q: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot open google.com. Which tool should you use to troubleshoot?
items.exp: nslookup or dig is used to query DNS servers and troubleshoot name resolution failures.

items.q: Which command displays all active TCP connections and listening ports on a host?
items.exp: netstat (Network Statistics) displays active connections, routing tables, and a number of network interface statistics.

items.q: OSI Layer 3
items.back: The Network Layer. Handles logical addressing (IP addresses) and routing of packets across multiple networks. Routers operate here.
items.analogy: Like the postal system sorting facility reading zip codes to determine which truck your package needs to go on.

items.q: OSI Layer 2 (Data Link)
items.back: Handles MAC addresses and switching. Protocols: Ethernet, ARP, STP. Devices: Switches.
items.analogy: The local neighborhood mail carrier who only knows physical street addresses (MACs).

items.q: OSI Layer 3 (Network)
items.back: Handles IP addresses and routing. Protocols: IP, ICMP, OSPF, BGP. Devices: Routers.
items.analogy: The postal sorting facility that routes mail to different states and countries using zip codes (IPs).

items.q: TCP vs UDP
items.back: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, and has error checking (HTTP, SSH). UDP is connectionless, fast, and unreliable (VoIP, Video).
items.analogy: TCP is certified mail with a return receipt. UDP is throwing a newspaper on a porch from a moving car.

items.q: DNS (Domain Name System)
items.back: Resolves human-readable domain names (google.com) to IP addresses (8.8.8.8). Runs on Port 53.
items.analogy: The phonebook of the internet. You look up a name to get the phone number.

items.q: VLAN (Virtual LAN)
items.back: Logically separates a physical switch into multiple isolated broadcast domains at Layer 2.
items.analogy: Taking one massive open-plan office and building soundproof walls to separate the departments.

items.q: STP (Spanning Tree Protocol)
items.back: Layer 2 protocol that prevents switching loops and broadcast storms by blocking redundant links.
items.analogy: A traffic cop who shuts down a roundabout entrance to prevent gridlock, but opens it if another road closes.

items.q: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol)
items.back: Used to monitor and configure network devices. Uses Agents, Managers, and MIBs. Port 161.
items.analogy: The dashboard in a car showing you exactly how the engine (router) is performing in real-time.

items.q: DHCP Snooping
items.back: A switch feature that drops DHCP offers from untrusted ports to prevent rogue DHCP server attacks.
items.analogy: A bouncer checking IDs to make sure nobody is handing out fake VIP passes in the club.

items.back: Automatic Private IP Addressing. Assigned by Windows when the client cannot reach a DHCP server.
items.analogy: The network equivalent of talking to yourself because nobody else is answering.

items.q: ping vs tracert
items.back: Ping tests basic reachability. Tracert/Traceroute shows the exact path of hops to the destination and where latency occurs.
items.analogy: Ping is asking 'Are you there?'. Tracert is asking 'Which exact roads did you take to get there and where was the traffic?'.
